title: Hosted API — Local Data Control Workflow and Audit Package Export
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and ship a hosted-API workflow that lets customers assert and enforce data locality and retention at the tenant and endpoint level, expose a retention policy composer in the Console, and generate a signed audit package (exportable evidence ZIP) that summarizes locality decisions, retention assignments, and event traces. The goal is to provide a single coherent flow for: (1) declaring locality constraints per tenant/route, (2) translating constraints to runtime routing and storage retention rules, (3) surfacing deterministic precedence and fallback behavior, and (4) producing a verifiable audit package suitable for compliance reviews. Deliverables: Console UI composer, API controls for policy attachment, operator mapping rules for routing engine, retention enforcement hooks, and an audit-export generator with tamper-evident signing.
comments: 2025-02-19 — Kickoff: PM + Eng meeting. Agreed to avoid modifying runtime routing DSL; instead introduce a thin mapping layer (policy -> routing rule) to minimize risk. Action: ENG to prototype mapping table. (Diego)

2025-02-24 — Design review: proposed Console composer mockups uploaded: https://drive.redwood/rdx/compliance/pm-31745/composer-v1.pdf. Feedback from Security: must include KMS key id for audit package signing and retention TTL metadata. (Maya)

2025-02-27 — Eng update: prototype mapping table implemented in branch https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/6243. It emits explicit region preference headers and fallbacks; initial tests show <2% routing divergence vs baseline. Need to add instrumentation to trace resolution path for audit logs. (Jules)

2025-03-01 — Trade-off discussion: two approaches evaluated for audit export signing: (A) sign JSON bundle server-side with platform KMS (fast, smaller scope), (B) produce signed manifest and let customer re-sign with their HSM for on-prem/private (larger scope). Decision: implement (A) now and design extension hooks for (B) in next iteration. (Maya)

2025-03-03 — QA plan: create synthetic tenants with mixed locality constraints and run 72h workload; verify that retention TTLs are applied to storage shards and that the audit package contains both the resolved policy map and per-request resolution trace. QA ticket planned: ENG-8579. (Diego)
